title: Transcoding a three-hour upload
description: Creators complain that a 3-hour lecture takes more than a day to become watchable, and a worker crash near the end restarts the job. Today one worker encodes the whole original into every rendition in sequence. What change best fixes processing latency and crash recovery?

options.text: Give the transcoding worker a larger machine with more CPU cores
options.explanation: Helps somewhat, but latency still scales with video length and a crash still loses all progress.

options.text: Run one job per rendition in parallel
options.explanation: Removes the sequential rendition loop, but each job is still as long as the video and a crash restarts hours of work.

options.text: Encode only the highest-quality rendition and let the CDN downscale on the fly
options.explanation: CDNs cache and serve bytes; they do not transcode per request, and viewers on slow networks would stall.

options.text: Split the original at keyframes into short chunks and run idempotent (chunk, rendition) encode tasks in parallel, with manifest assembly as a fan-in step
options.explanation: Per-video latency becomes roughly one chunk's encode time plus orchestration, and a failed task retries only its chunk because outputs have deterministic keys.
